mcqs.stem: Best guess: in a like-kind exchange of real property with no boot, what is the basis of the property received?

choices.text: The basis of the property given
choices.explanation: Correct. Substituted basis preserves the deferred gain.

choices.text: The average of the two FMVs

choices.explanation: That would ignore the deferred gain.

mcqs.explanation: Substituted basis preserves the deferred gain.

mcqs.stem: Land (basis $40,000) is sold for $200,000: $50,000 down and $150,000 next year. No liabilities or recapture. How much gain is recognized in the year of sale?

choices.explanation: Only the gross profit share of the payment.

mcqs.stem: Which exchange qualifies under §1031 in 2025?

choices.text: A delivery truck for another delivery truck
Investment farmland for a rental apartment building
choices.explanation: Correct. Real property held for business or investment is like-kind to other such real property.

choices.text: A developer's lots held for sale for a warehouse
Stock in one company for stock in another

mcqs.explanation: Real property held for business or investment is like-kind to other such real property.

mcqs.stem: A property (basis $120,000) is sold for $300,000: the buyer assumes a $60,000 mortgage and pays the rest over 5 years, starting next year. What is the contract price?
mcqs.explanation: Contract price = selling price − liabilities assumed (not exceeding basis).

mcqs.stem: Using the facts above (gain $180,000; contract price $240,000), how much gain is recognized when a $48,000 payment is received?
Which sale can use the installment method?

choices.text: A retailer's sale of inventory on credit terms
Sale of publicly traded stock on an exchange
An individual's land sale with payments over 4 years
choices.explanation: Correct. Casual sales of non-inventory property qualify.
Recapture is recognized in the year of sale.

mcqs.explanation: Casual sales of non-inventory property qualify.

mcqs.stem: In a §1031 exchange, Jo gives land (basis $80,000, FMV $150,000) and receives land worth $130,000 plus $20,000 cash. What is the recognized gain and new basis?

choices.explanation: Adds the boot instead of subtracting it.

mcqs.stem: In a §1031 exchange, Max gives property subject to a $100,000 mortgage and takes property subject to a $70,000 mortgage; no cash. His realized gain is $200,000. What gain does he recognize?
mcqs.explanation: Net liability relief (100,000 − 70,000) is boot received.

mcqs.stem: What are the deadlines in a deferred (delayed) like-kind exchange?

choices.text: Identify within 45 days; receive within 180 days
Identify within 30 days; receive within 90 days
Identify within 60 days; receive within 1 year
No deadlines apply if a qualified intermediary is used

mcqs.explanation: §1031(a)(3): 45-day identification and 180-day exchange periods.

mcqs.stem: A mother sells stock (basis $50,000) to her son for $30,000. The son later sells it for $45,000. What are the results?

choices.text: Mother's loss disallowed; son has $15,000 gain
choices.explanation: The disallowed loss offsets his later gain.

choices.text: Mother's loss disallowed; son has no gain
choices.explanation: Correct. His $15,000 gain is offset by the disallowed loss.

choices.text: Mother deducts $20,000; son has no gain
choices.explanation: The mother's loss is disallowed under §267.

mcqs.explanation: §267(d): the buyer's gain is reduced by the previously disallowed loss (to the extent of the gain).

mcqs.stem: An individual sells depreciable equipment at a $40,000 gain (no depreciation taken) to a corporation she owns 70% of. What is the character of the gain?

choices.explanation: Correct. §1239: gain on depreciable property sold to a more-than-50%-owned entity is ordinary.

mcqs.explanation: §1239: gain on depreciable property sold to a more-than-50%-owned entity is ordinary.

mcqs.stem: Brothers exchange rental properties under §1031. Eighteen months later, one brother sells the property he received. What happens?

choices.text: Only the selling brother recognizes his gain
choices.explanation: The deferred exchange gain is also triggered.

choices.text: Both brothers recognize their deferred gain
choices.explanation: Correct. §1031(f): a disposition within 2 years by either related party triggers the deferred gain.

mcqs.explanation: §1031(f): a disposition within 2 years by either related party triggers the deferred gain.

mcqs.stem: A seller holds a $10 million installment note at year-end (sale price over $150,000). What additional rule applies?

choices.text: The note must be reported at fair market value
Recapture is deferred along with the gain
The installment method is disallowed entirely
choices.explanation: It's allowed with an interest charge.

choices.text: Interest on the deferred tax above $5 million
choices.explanation: Correct. §453A imposes interest on the deferred tax when installment obligations exceed $5 million at year-end.

mcqs.explanation: §453A imposes interest on the deferred tax when installment obligations exceed $5 million at year-end.

mcqs.stem: A warehouse (adjusted basis $300,000) is destroyed by fire, and the owner receives $500,000 of insurance proceeds. Within the replacement period she buys a replacement warehouse for $450,000. What gain is recognized, and what is the basis of the new warehouse?

choices.explanation: Gain is deferred to the extent the proceeds are reinvested.
The 50,000 not reinvested must be recognized.
Basis is reduced by the 150,000 deferred gain.
Correct. Realized gain 200,000; recognized = proceeds not reinvested (50,000); deferred 150,000; basis = 450,000 − 150,000 = 300,000.

mcqs.explanation: §1033: recognize the lesser of realized gain or unreinvested proceeds; replacement basis = cost − deferred gain.

mcqs.stem: Ken owns 30% of X Corp. His father owns 25%, his brother-in-law owns 20%, and a partnership in which Ken is a 50% partner owns 10%. What percentage of X Corp does Ken own under §267(c)?

choices.explanation: Correct. Ken's 30% + father's 25% (family) + 50% of the partnership's 10% (5%) = 60%. A brother-in-law is not family under §267.
In-laws are not family members for §267.
This leaves out the stock owned through the partnership.
This leaves out the father's stock, which is attributed to Ken.

mcqs.explanation: §267(c): family (spouse, ancestors, lineal descendants, siblings) and proportionate entity attribution.

mcqs.stem: A company's business real property is condemned. How long does it have to buy replacement property to defer gain?

choices.explanation: Correct. Condemned business real property gets 3 years.

mcqs.explanation: §1033(g)(4): the replacement period is 3 years for condemned business or investment real property (2 years otherwise).

mcqs.stem: A business trades old equipment for new equipment of the same type. Can it defer the gain under §1031?

choices.explanation: Correct. Since 2018 personal property is excluded.

choices.text: Yes, if held for over a year
Only for trucks and other vehicles

mcqs.explanation: Since 2018, §1031 applies only to exchanges of real property held for business or investment.

mcqs.stem: A father sells land to his son on the installment method. Eight months later, the son resells it for cash. What is the effect on the father?

choices.text: No effect on the father's sale
Only the son recognizes any gain

choices.explanation: Correct. The resale within 2 years triggers recognition.

mcqs.explanation: §453(e): if a related buyer resells within 2 years, the original seller treats the resale proceeds as received.

mcqs.stem: In a like-kind exchange, a taxpayer gives land (basis $100,000) plus $30,000 cash for land worth $150,000. What is the basis of the new land?

choices.explanation: Correct. Old basis plus cash paid.

mcqs.explanation: Basis of property received = basis given up + boot paid + gain recognized − boot received.

mcqs.stem: In a deferred like-kind exchange, why does a seller use a qualified intermediary?

choices.explanation: Correct. Receiving cash would make it taxable.

mcqs.explanation: A qualified intermediary holds sale proceeds so the taxpayer doesn't constructively receive them.

mcqs.stem: A business owner-user's factory is destroyed. To defer gain under §1033, what replacement property is required?

choices.text: Similar or related in service or use
choices.explanation: Correct. A functional-use test for owner-users.

choices.text: Property of equal or greater cost only

mcqs.explanation: For owner-users, replacement must be similar or related in service or use; the broader like-kind test applies to condemned real property.

mcqs.stem: A seller pledges an installment note as collateral for a bank loan. What is the effect?

choices.text: No effect on the installment method
The loan proceeds count as payment

mcqs.explanation: §453A(d): pledging an installment obligation as security treats the loan proceeds as a payment on the note.

mcqs.stem: Can U.S. real property be exchanged tax-free under §1031 for real property in France?

choices.text: Yes, all real property is like-kind

choices.explanation: That isn't what the rule says.
Correct. U.S. and foreign real property aren't like-kind.

mcqs.explanation: Real property in the U.S. and real property outside the U.S. aren't like-kind.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer gives land (basis $200,000; FMV $300,000) plus $20,000 cash for like-kind land worth $320,000. What gain is recognized, and what is the new basis?

choices.explanation: Correct. Paying boot doesn't trigger gain.

mcqs.stem: Land with a $100,000 basis is sold for $400,000: the buyer assumes a $150,000 mortgage, pays $30,000 down and gives a note. How much gain is recognized in the year of sale?

choices.explanation: Only the excess is a payment.
Correct. The $50,000 of mortgage over basis is a deemed payment; the gross profit percentage is 100%.

mcqs.explanation: Contract price = 400,000 − 150,000 + 50,000 = 300,000; gross profit 300,000; ratio 100%; year-1 payments 30,000 + 50,000.

mcqs.stem: Brothers exchange like-kind properties. One brother dies 14 months later, and his estate sells the property. Is the other brother's deferred gain triggered?

choices.explanation: That isn't what the rule says.

choices.text: Only if the estate sells at a gain
choices.explanation: That isn't what the rule says.
Correct. Dispositions due to death don't accelerate gain.

mcqs.explanation: The related-party 2-year rule doesn't apply to dispositions after the death of either party.

mcqs.stem: What deadlines apply to a deferred §1031 exchange?

choices.text: 60 days to identify; 1 year to close

mcqs.explanation: Replacement property must be identified within 45 days and received within 180 days (or the return due date).

mcqs.stem: Within how many days must QSBS sale proceeds be reinvested for a §1045 rollover?
mcqs.explanation: §1045 defers gain on QSBS held over 6 months if proceeds are reinvested in QSBS within 60 days.

mcqs.stem: Which sale can't use the installment method?

choices.text: Sale of land to an individual

mcqs.explanation: The installment method isn't available for dealer sales, inventory or publicly traded securities.

mcqs.stem: Property worth $500,000 (basis $300,000) is exchanged for like-kind property worth $450,000 plus $50,000 cash. What is the gain recognized and the new basis?

choices.explanation: Boot is taxed in this case.

mcqs.explanation: Gain is recognized to the extent of boot; the new basis is old basis plus gain less boot.

mcqs.stem: Property worth $400,000 (basis $250,000, mortgage $100,000 assumed by the buyer) is exchanged for debt-free like-kind property worth $300,000. What gain is recognized?

choices.explanation: Only the boot in this case.

mcqs.explanation: Net liability relief is treated as boot received.

mcqs.stem: In the exchange above ($250,000 basis, $100,000 gain recognized, $100,000 of liability relief), what is the basis of the new property?
mcqs.explanation: New basis equals FMV less deferred gain: $300,000 − $50,000.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer gives up property with a $100,000 mortgage and assumes a $120,000 mortgage on the replacement. No cash changes hands. What gain is recognized?
mcqs.explanation: Liabilities given up and assumed are netted; assuming more debt isn't boot received.

mcqs.stem: A building (basis $200,000) is destroyed, and $350,000 of insurance is received. $320,000 is reinvested in similar property. What is the gain recognized and the new basis?
mcqs.explanation: Under §1033, gain is recognized to the extent proceeds aren't reinvested; deferred gain reduces new basis.

mcqs.stem: Land (basis $100,000) is sold for $400,000: $100,000 down, plus a $300,000 note paid over 3 years. What gain is recognized in year 1?
mcqs.explanation: Installment gain equals payments received times the gross profit ratio.

mcqs.stem: When does an interest charge on deferred tax apply to installment obligations?
mcqs.explanation: An interest charge applies when installment obligations from sales over $150,000 exceed $5 million at year-end.

mcqs.stem: A parent sells land to her son on the installment method. He resells it 18 months later for cash. What happens?

choices.explanation: Correct. The related-party resale rule applies.

choices.text: The son reports the parent's gain

mcqs.explanation: If a related buyer resells within 2 years, the original seller recognizes the deferred gain.

mcqs.stem: QSBS held 8 months with a $200,000 basis is sold for $1,000,000. $900,000 is reinvested in new QSBS within 60 days. What gain is recognized?
mcqs.explanation: §1045 recognizes gain only to the extent proceeds exceed the cost of replacement QSBS.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer exchanges a life insurance policy for an annuity contract. How is it treated?
mcqs.explanation: §1035 allows tax-free exchanges of life insurance for annuities and similar contracts.

mcqs.stem: Brothers exchange like-kind rental properties. One sells his new property 15 months later. What happens?

choices.text: Only the seller's gain is triggered

mcqs.explanation: If either related party disposes of the property within 2 years, both deferred gains are recognized.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer wants to buy replacement property before selling the old property. What structure allows a §1031 exchange?

choices.text: A reverse exchange using an EAT

mcqs.explanation: A reverse exchange uses an exchange accommodation titleholder to park property within the time limits.

mcqs.stem: In 2025, a business trades in a truck (basis $10,000, trade-in value $25,000) for a new truck. What is recognized?

choices.explanation: Correct. Personal property doesn't qualify for §1031.
It's a gain in this case.

mcqs.explanation: Since 2018, like-kind exchange treatment applies only to real property.

mcqs.stem: In 2025, a taxpayer invests a capital gain in a qualified opportunity fund under the original rules. How long is the gain deferred?
mcqs.explanation: Gains invested under the original rules are deferred until the earlier of sale or December 31, 2026.

mcqs.stem: An investor wants to sell an appreciated apartment building and stay invested in real estate. What should she consider?
mcqs.explanation: A deferred exchange through a qualified intermediary defers gain if the property is reinvested.

mcqs.stem: An investor's relinquished property has a large mortgage. How can she avoid boot?

choices.text: Pay off the old debt with exchange funds
Buy property with equal or more debt

mcqs.explanation: Acquiring equal or greater debt, or adding cash, offsets liability relief.

mcqs.stem: A seller wants to spread gain across several tax years, and the buyer can't pay all cash. What fits?

choices.explanation: The buyer has cash, not property.
Not a sale in this case.

mcqs.explanation: Installment sales defer gain until payments are received.

mcqs.stem: An owner wants to dispose of a rental that has declined in value below basis. Should she do a §1031 exchange?
mcqs.explanation: Like-kind exchanges defer losses as well as gains, so loss property is usually sold.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer's real property is condemned. How broad is the replacement standard?

choices.explanation: Correct. A broader standard for condemnations.

mcqs.explanation: For condemned business or investment real property, like-kind replacement property qualifies.

mcqs.stem: What is a long-term cost of deferring gain through a §1031 exchange?

choices.explanation: It defers tax in this case.

mcqs.explanation: Carryover basis means less depreciation on the replacement property.

mcqs.stem: An individual sells land (basis $90,000) for $300,000: $60,000 down in 2025 and $240,000 in 2027. No liabilities. How much gain is recognized in 2025?
In a §1031 exchange, E gives property (basis $200,000; FMV $500,000) and $40,000 cash for property worth $540,000. What is E's recognized gain and new basis?
mcqs.explanation: No boot received; basis = 200,000 + 40,000.

mcqs.stem: A father sells land (basis $100,000) to his daughter for $70,000. She later sells it for $90,000. What is her recognized gain?

choices.explanation: The disallowed loss offsets her gain.
Correct. §267(d): her 20,000 gain is reduced by the father's 30,000 disallowed loss (not below zero).
Her gain can't become a loss.

mcqs.explanation: §267(d): her 20,000 gain is reduced by the father's 30,000 disallowed loss (not below zero).

mcqs.stem: Which transaction can use the installment method?

choices.text: An individual's sale of a rental building, paid over 10 years
choices.explanation: Correct. Non-dealer sales of real property qualify.

choices.text: A dealer's sale of subdivided lots
A sale of publicly traded stock
Sale of depreciable property to a 60%-owned corporation
choices.explanation: §453(g) bars it for related depreciable property.

mcqs.explanation: Non-dealer sales of real property qualify.

mcqs.stem: In a like-kind exchange, a taxpayer gives real property (basis $80,000; FMV $150,000) and receives real property (FMV $140,000) plus $10,000 cash. What gain is recognized?

choices.explanation: Correct. Recognized gain = lesser of realized 70,000 or boot 10,000.

mcqs.explanation: Recognized gain = lesser of realized 70,000 or boot 10,000.

mcqs.stem: Which property can qualify for a §1031 like-kind exchange in 2025?

choices.explanation: Correct. Only real property held for business or investment qualifies.
Not held for business or investment.
Property held for sale is excluded.

mcqs.explanation: Only real property held for business or investment qualifies.

mcqs.stem: A taxpayer sells investment land (basis $200,000) for $500,000: $100,000 down in 2025 and the rest in later years, with adequate interest. How much gain is recognized in 2025 under the installment method?

choices.explanation: Only the gross profit portion of the payment is gain.
That is the return of basis portion.

mcqs.explanation: IRC §453: gain recognized = payments received × gross profit ratio.

mcqs.stem: In a like-kind exchange of real property, a taxpayer gives property worth $300,000 (basis $180,000) and receives property worth $260,000 plus $40,000 cash. What gain is recognized, and what is the basis of the new property?

choices.explanation: Correct. Gain is the lesser of realized gain (120,000) or boot (40,000); basis = 180,000 + 40,000 − 40,000.

mcqs.explanation: IRC §1031: recognized gain = lesser of realized gain or boot received; new basis = old basis + gain recognized − boot received.

mcqs.stem: A business's warehouse (not condemned) is destroyed by fire in 2025, and insurance proceeds exceed basis. Within what period must it buy qualified replacement property to defer the gain under §1033?

choices.explanation: 180 days is a like-kind exchange deadline.
The period is two years after year-end.

choices.text: Five years after the end of the tax year
Two years after that tax year ends
choices.explanation: Correct. The general replacement period is two years (three for condemned business real property).

mcqs.explanation: IRC §1033(a)(2)(B): replacement must occur within two years after the close of the first tax year in which any gain is realized (three years for condemned real property held for business or investment).

mcqs.stem: Two brothers exchange like-kind real property. Eighteen months later, one brother sells the property he received. What happens?

choices.text: Only the selling brother recognizes gain
Both recognize their deferred gain that year
choices.explanation: Correct. §1031(f) requires related parties to hold for two years.

choices.text: Nothing; the exchange was already complete
The original exchange is amended retroactively
choices.explanation: Gain is recognized in the year of the disposition.

mcqs.explanation: IRC §1031(f): if either related party disposes of the property within two years, the deferred gain is recognized as of the date of that disposition.

mcqs.stem: Equipment with $25,000 of §1245 recapture is sold on the installment method for a $40,000 total gain. How much gain is recognized in the year of sale, before applying the gross profit ratio to the remaining gain?

choices.explanation: Correct. Depreciation recapture is recognized in the year of sale regardless of payments.

mcqs.explanation: IRC §453(i): recapture income is recognized in the year of disposition; the remaining gain is reported under the installment method.

flashcards.back: Gross profit ÷ contract price (selling price − liabilities assumed, not above basis).
Recognized in full in the year of sale.
Real property held for business or investment only.
Identify within 45 days; complete within 180 days.
FMV of new property − deferred gain.
Related-party losses disallowed; buyer's later gain reduced.
Related-party exchange; disposition within 2 years triggers deferred gain.
